TaskSquad · Native iOS · 28 October 2026

Usability changes, implemented and retested

Required actions are clearer, secondary options stay out of the way, and reading and replying now share one surface. Review the before/after screenshots and exact verification scope below.

Small issue-specific local commitsAPI contracts preservedThree existing simulators
ChangesVerificationBefore / afterKeyboardCommits

What changed

  1. Task creation: persistent required/optional labels, focused field errors, one Attach menu with previews, Send later, and collapsed Advanced controls.
  2. Draft recovery: images and text survive cancellation and relaunch. Successful sends remove the draft; failed sends retain it.
  3. Reading and replying: compact metadata, inline replies, visible note Edit, document-first notes, expandable tool details, and bounded reading width on larger screens.
  4. Navigation and inbox: grouped destinations, pinned project/account access, direct project switching, a named Library selector, visible status filters and clearable no-results states.
  5. Schedules and terminal: native time/timezone selectors, relevant day controls, 44pt terminal targets and accessible arrow-key names.

The current list API does not expose message previews, unread counts or complete project totals. Those were not invented. Search and filters still apply to loaded records. The proposed bottom tab bar remains a separate prototype.

The full run includes task creation, image round trips, authentication/logout, role/project isolation, all destinations, navigation recovery, dark/large text, terminal lifecycle and the added usability journeys. Shared Swift regression tests passed in every contract invocation. The optional promotional capture accounts for the one skip.

The final reply run rechecks image upload, cancellation/relaunch, failed-send retry and cleanup after the final Send-contrast and typing-layout corrections. Focused runs repeat some full-run tests; their counts are not additional unique journeys.

Remaining diagnostics: iOS 26.1 runs still record frame-dimension and view-reparenting warnings; the root cause is not established. The iOS 17.2 small-phone run recorded no runtime warnings. Hosted tests also log duplicate Swift class loading warnings. Passing assertions do not mean these diagnostics are fixed.

Not qualified here: manual VoiceOver traversal, accessibility-size keyboard layouts, iPad landscape keyboard behavior, realistic long datasets, offline networking, and a live production account/daemon. These fixture tests do not measure user completion speed.
